subject: Altiora onboarding: GPU pool scaling, autoscale/burst decisions & region selection
messages:
From: Jared Lin <jared@altiora.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for Altiora onboarding

Hi Ben / Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. I promised to send some high-level context so we can lock down regional choices and autoscale behaviour before SOW. Quick points: 

- Production traffic today: see attached (30d aggregate). Peak concurrent gen calls ~1800 reqs/min, 95th token length ~420 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for user-facing flows; background batch can tolerate higher latency.
- Data residency: core inference must stay in US/EU; no APAC requirement for now but traffic originates globally.
- Burst windows: we have daily spikes around APAC evening and occasional marketing-driven spikes (1-2 hours) that can be 2.5x baseline.

Could Redwood share your recommended pool sizing and burst approach for a pilot (production toggle to dedicated after pilot)? Also curious on cold-start behavior with prefix cache and typical warmup recommendations.

Appreciate it — Jared

Attachment: Altiora_current_traffic.csv (text/csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jared Lin <jared@altiora.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for Altiora onboarding

Jared — thanks for the data, that helps a lot. High-level responses and next steps below.

Summary answers: 
- Pilot sizing: for your current peaks (~1800 reqs/min) and p95 target, we recommend starting with a 6-GPU dedicated pool (A100-equivalent) with a warm pool of 2 extra cards for burst. That gives headroom for 2x short spikes while keeping p95 under target.
- Autoscale/burst model: we propose a two-tier policy — steady autoscale target for baseline traffic with fast burst capacity (pre-warmed instances) for marketing spikes. Burst will be billed based on a short-term premium; we'll document exact burn rates in the MAP.
- Cold-starts and KV/prefix caching: best practice is to pre-warm KV cache for commonly used prompts during business hours; cold-starts on a new model variant take ~4–6s for first warmup unless we replicate KV layers. We'll include a warmup script in the onboarding repo.

Next steps: 
1) Internal scoping call to confirm model variants, tokenization profiles, and SLO enforcement rules (can we do 10/21 10am PT?).
2) Monica/Sean will draft the MAP and a draft pool topology for your review.
3) Jared to confirm whether EU residency is required for inference (you mentioned core must stay in US/EU).

I'll loop in Sean to draft the operational runbook.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for Altiora onboarding

Ben / Sean / Kimberly — taking Ben's recommendations and sketching an ops-first topology for the MAP (internal). Key points and risks: 

- Recommended topology: Primary US pool (6 GPUs), standby EU pool (2 GPUs hot for residency) with cross-region failover. APAC: no dedicated pool initially; use regional hosted endpoints + burst routing to US for cost control.
- Burst strategy: maintain 2 pre-warmed GPUs in US pool (kept warm via low-cost warmup queries). Configure autoscale thresholds: scale up at sustained 70% GPU utilization for 90s; emergency burst policy for 150% of baseline using warm pool.
- Cost/latency trade-off: cross-region routing will add ~40–80ms for APAC-origin traffic if served from US — acceptable if within p95 budget. Recommend monitoring cohort by region for 2 weeks post-cutover.
- Operational hooks: 1) Model pinning per route, 2) Canary traffic at 5% for each rollout, 3) automated rollback on quality regression.

Action items (internal):
- Sean to write the runbook steps for warm pool lifecycle and warmup scripts.
- Kimberly to prepare the SLO enforcement config and billing impact note for the deal team.
- Ben to send MAP draft to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

Monica
Head of CS Implementation
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Lin <jared@altiora.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for Altiora onboarding

Thanks — this looks good. Quick clarifications: 
- EU residency: yes, we need model inference for EU customer subset (approx 18% of traffic) to stay within EU datacenters.
- Warm pool: happy to accept 2 pre-warmed GPUs for initial pilot. Please include estimated burn rate.
- Pilot go-live: aiming for 10/30. Can the pilot run for 4 weeks with escalation criteria defined?

Sending a second attachment with a 7-day hourly breakdown so you get the spike patterns.

Jared
Ops Lead, Altiora
Attachment: Altiora_hourly_7day.csv (text/csv)

Date: Sat, 22 Sep 2028 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Altiora MAP draft and proposed runbook

Jared — attaching the first draft of the MAP (mutual action plan) and a short ops runbook excerpt. Highlights:

- Pilot topology: US primary pool (6 GPUs) + EU residency pool (2 GPUs hot); APAC to use hosted routing to US for pilot.
- Timeline:
  * 10/05: Discovery call (model variants, tokenization specifics)
  * 10/12: Runbook + warmup scripts delivered to Altiora repo
  * 10/19: Dry-run traffic validation on staging
  * 10/30: Pilot go-live (4-week pilot window)
- Success criteria: p95 <= 350ms for user-facing routes, no more than 3 unplanned rollbacks during pilot, and cost burn within 20% of estimated MAP numbers.

See attached: MAP_Altiora_v1.pdf and small runbook excerpt included inline. Please review and flag any missing items.

Next internal steps: Kimberly to finalize cost estimate and Sean to complete warmup script checklist.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
